title: Two Big Leaders Meet: Xi and Trump Agree on AI Hotline
summary: Imagine two of the biggest countries in the world — the United States and China — sitting down for a three-day meeting in Washington, D.C. That's exactly what happened. President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping shook hands and agreed to set up a special hotline for AI problems. If something goes wrong with artificial intelligence, the two countries can talk fast instead of guessing. They also agreed to keep talking about their armies, so small problems don't turn into big ones. On trade, they agreed to keep a two-month pause on some tariffs (taxes on goods that travel between countries). China even said it will buy at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the U.S. in 2027 and 2028. That's a lot of coal — about the weight of 100,000 school buses! Trump said the U.S. won't slow down its AI work. "We're leading by at least a year," he told reporters. The two sides will meet again in Shenzhen, China, in November. No giant breakthroughs, but experts say the new hotlines are a big deal.
why_it_matters: When the world's two biggest countries can talk quickly instead of guessing, it can mean fewer misunderstandings that could affect jobs, prices, and peace for families everywhere.

keywords.explanation: A special phone line that lets leaders talk to each other very fast in an emergency.
Computer programs that can think, learn, or solve problems in ways that seem smart.
Taxes a country puts on goods that come in from another country.
A short stop before things start again.
A way to measure heavy things — one metric ton is about as heavy as a small car.
People who know a lot about one subject and study it closely.

background_read: The United States and China are the two biggest economies in the world, and they often disagree about trade and technology — so when their leaders meet, the whole world watches.
Xi Jinping (China's top leader) and Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) sat down together for three days.

Special 'hotlines' between rival countries are an old idea: during the Cold War, the U.S. and the Soviet Union set up a direct phone link so their leaders could talk fast during a scary moment instead of guessing.
Shenzhen (a huge city in southern China known for making electronics) will host the next meeting.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump of the United States and President Xi Jinping of China, meeting with their teams.
WHAT: They agreed on a hotline for AI problems, keeping talks going about their armies, and a two-month pause on some tariffs; China will buy at least 10 million metric tons of U.S. coal.
WHERE: The meeting was in Washington, D.C.; the next meeting is in Shenzhen, China, in November.
WHY: So small problems don't turn into big ones, and so both countries can talk fast if something goes wrong with AI.

perspectives.description: The two leaders met face to face for three days and set up fast ways to talk, which supporters say can stop small arguments from growing into big ones.
Some people point out there were no giant breakthroughs; the big disagreements about trade and technology are still there, and buying coal may not help the planet.
Experts say meetings like this are less about becoming friends and more about keeping a competition calm and predictable.
